metadata.title: Forking and stability in the representations of a $C^*$-algebra

nodes.name: The metric structure $(H,\p)$
nodes.statement: Recall that we include a symbol $\dot{a}$ in the language of the Hilbert space structure whose interpretation in $H$ will be $\p(a)$ for every $a$ in the unit ball of $\A$ getting the following metric structure of only one sort: \[(Ball_1(H),0,-,i,\half[x+y],\|\cdot\|,(\p(a))_{a\in Ball_1(\A)})\] where $Ball_1(H)$ and $Ball_1(\A)$ are the corresponding unit balls in $H$ and $\A$ respectively; $0$ is the zero vector in $H$; $-: Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to any vector $v\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $-v$; $i: Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to any vector $v\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $iv$ where $i^2=-1$; $\half[x+y]: Ball_1(H)\times Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to a couple of vectors $v$, $w\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $\half[v+w]$; $\|\cdot\|: Ball_1(H) \to [0, 1]$ is the norm function; $\A$ is an unital $C^*$-algebra; $\p:\A\to B(H)$ is a $C^*$-algebra isometric homomorphism. The metric is given by $d(v,w) =\|\half[v-w]\|$. Briefly, the structure will be refered to as $(H,\p)$.
nodes.statement_short: One-sorted metric structure on the unit ball of $H$ with a symbol for each $\p(a)$, $a\in Ball_1(\A)$.
nodes.genus: metric structure of only one sort
nodes.origin_citation: Argoty, The model theory of modules of a $C^*$-algebra [Ar]

nodes.name: The positive linear functional $\f_v$
nodes.statement: Here, $\f_v:\A\to\C$ is the positive linear functional defined by the formula $\f_v(a)=\langle av\ |\ v\rangle$.
differentia: defined by the formula $\f_v(a)=\langle av\ |\ v\rangle$

nodes.name: Quantifier elimination for $Th(H,\p)$
nodes.statement: The theory of $(H,\p)$ has quantifier elimination. Furthermore, for $v,w\in H$, $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\f_v=\f_w$.
nodes.statement_short: The theory has quantifier elimination and types over $\emptyset$ are classified by the functional $\f_v$.
conclusions: The theory of $(H,\p)$ has quantifier elimination
$tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\f_v=\f_w$

nodes.name: Notation: $H_E$, $\p_E$ and the subrepresentation generated by $E$
nodes.statement: Given $E\subseteq H$ and $v\in H$, we denote by: \bitm \item $H_E$, the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by the elements $\p(a)v$, where $v\in E$ and $a\in\A$. \item $\p_E:=\{\p(a)\upharpoonright H_E\ |\ a\in \A\}$. \item $(H_E,\p_E)$, the subrepresentation of $(H,\p)$ generated by $E$. \item $H_v$, the space $H_E$ when $E=\{v\}$ for some vector $v\in H$. \item $\p_v:=\p_E$ when $E=\{v\}$. \item $(H_v,\p_v)$, the subrepresentation of $(H,\p)$ generated by $v$. \item $(H,\p,v)$, means that $\{\p(a)v\ |\ a\in\A\}$ is dense in $(H,\p)$. \item $H_E^\perp$, the orthogonal complement of $H_E$. \item $P_E$, the projection over $H_E$. \item $P_{E^\perp}$, the projection over $H_E^\perp$. \eitm
nodes.statement_short: Notation for the subrepresentation $(H_E,\p_E)$ generated by a set $E$, its cyclic case $(H_v,\p_v)$, and the associated projections.

nodes.name: Essential and discrete parts of $\p$, $\p(\A)$, $H$, vectors and sets
nodes.statement: Given a representation $\p:\A\to B(H)$, we define: \bitm \item The \textit{essential part} of $\p$ is the $C^*$-algebra homomorphism, \[\p_e:=\r\circ\p:\A\to B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)\] of $\p(\A)$, where $\r$ is the canonical proyection of $B(H)$ onto the Calkin Algebra $B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)$. \item The \textit{discrete part} of $\p$ is the restriction, \begin{align*} \p_d:ker(\p_e)&\to \mathcal{K}(H)\\ a &\to \p(a) \end{align*} \item The \textit{discrete part} of $\p(\A)$ is defined in the following way: \[\p(\A)_d:=\p(\A)\cap \mathcal{K}(H).\] \item The \textit{essential part} of $\p(\A)$ is the image $\p(\A)_e$ of $\p(\A)$ in the Calkin Algebra. \item The \textit{essential part} of $H$ is defined in the following way: \[H_e:=\text{ker}(\p(\A)_d)\] \item The \textit{discrete part} of $H$ is defined in the following way: \[H_d:=\text{ker}(\p(\A)_d)^\perp\] \item The \textit{essential part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_e$ of $v$ over $H_e$. \item The \textit{discrete part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_d$ of $v$ over $H_d$. \item The \textit{essential part} of a set $E\subseteq H$ is the set \[E_e:=\{v_e\ |\ v\in E\}\] \item The \textit{discrete part} of a set $G\subseteq H$ is the set \[E_d:=\{v_d\ |\ v\in G\}\] \eitm
nodes.statement_short: Essential part = image in the Calkin algebra (with $H_e=\text{ker}(\p(\A)_d)$); discrete part = compact part, with $H_d=H_e^\perp$; extended to vectors and sets.

nodes.name: Characterization of $\Aut((H,\p)/E)$
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$, $U\in \Aut(H,\p)$. Then $U\in \Aut((H,\p)/E)$ if and only if: \bitm \item For all $v\in H$ and all $a\in\A$, $U(\p(a)(v))=\p(a)(Uv)$. \item For all $w\in H_E$, $Uw=w$. \eitm
nodes.statement_short: An automorphism fixes $E$ iff it commutes with the representation and is the identity on $H_E$.
conclusions: For all $v\in H$ and all $a\in\A$, $U(\p(a)(v))=\p(a)(Uv)$.
For all $w\in H_E$, $Uw=w$.

nodes.name: $(H,\p)\equiv (H,\p)\oplus(H_e,\p_e)$
nodes.statement: For any index set $I$, $(H,\p)\equiv (H,\p)\oplus(H_e,\p_e)$.
conclusions: $(H,\p)\equiv (H,\p)\oplus(H_e,\p_e)$

nodes.name: Vectors in $H_e$ are not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H_e$. Then $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$

nodes.name: Proof that $v\in H_e$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $\k>2^{\aleph_0}$ and consider $(H,\p)\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in I}(H_e,\p_e)$. By Corollary \ref{CoroElementaryEquivalent}. Then there are $\k$ vectors $v_i$ for $i<\k$ such that every $v_i$ has the same type over $\emptyset$ as $v$. This means that the orbit of $v$ under the automorphisms of $(H,\p)$ is unbounded and therefore $v$ is not algebraic over the emptyset.
nodes.statement_short: Take a large direct sum of copies of the essential part to make the orbit of $v$ unbounded.

nodes.name: Pass to a large direct sum
nodes.statement: Let $\k>2^{\aleph_0}$ and consider $(H,\p)\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in I}(H_e,\p_e)$. By Corollary \ref{CoroElementaryEquivalent}. Then there are $\k$ vectors $v_i$ for $i<\k$ such that every $v_i$ has the same type over $\emptyset$ as $v$.
nodes.statement_short: Build $\k>2^{\aleph_0}$ realizations of $tp(v/\emptyset)$ in an elementary extension.

nodes.name: Conclude the orbit is unbounded
nodes.statement: This means that the orbit of $v$ under the automorphisms of $(H,\p)$ is unbounded and therefore $v$ is not algebraic over the emptyset.
nodes.statement_short: Unbounded orbit implies non-algebraicity.

nodes.name: Vectors in $H_d$ are algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H_d$. Then $v$ is algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is algebraic over $\emptyset$

nodes.name: $v_e\neq 0$ implies $v$ not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ such that $v_e\neq 0$. Then $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$

nodes.name: Proof that $v_e\neq 0$ implies $v$ is not algebraic
nodes.statement: Clear from previous Lemma \ref{Henotalgebraicoveremptyset}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the previous lemma on $H_e$.

nodes.name: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
nodes.statement: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
conclusions: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$

nodes.name: Proof of $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset}, $H_d\subseteq acl(\emptyset)$ and, by Lemma \ref{LemmaIfVeNotZeroVNotAlgebraic}, $acl(\emptyset)\subseteq H_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Double inclusion, one from each of the two preceding results.

nodes.name: Characterization of $acl(E)$
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Then $acl(E)$ is the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$.
conclusions: $acl(E)$ is the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$

nodes.name: Proof of the characterization of $acl(E)$
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$. It is clear that $G\subseteq acl(E)$. Let $v\in acl(E)$. By Lemma \ref{Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset}, $v_d\in acl(\emptyset)$, and by Theorem \ref{definclosure} and Lemma \ref{Henotalgebraicoveremptyset}, $v_e\in dcl(E)\setminus acl(\emptyset)$. Then $v_e\in dcl(E)$ and $acl(E)\subseteq G$.
nodes.statement_short: Double inclusion, splitting $v\in acl(E)$ into its discrete and essential parts.

nodes.name: Set up $G$ and the easy inclusion
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$. It is clear that $G\subseteq acl(E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $G$ and note $G\subseteq acl(E)$.

nodes.name: Reverse inclusion via the $v_d$/$v_e$ splitting
nodes.statement: Let $v\in acl(E)$. By Lemma \ref{Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset}, $v_d\in acl(\emptyset)$, and by Theorem \ref{definclosure} and Lemma \ref{Henotalgebraicoveremptyset}, $v_e\in dcl(E)\setminus acl(\emptyset)$. Then $v_e\in dcl(E)$ and $acl(E)\subseteq G$.
nodes.statement_short: Split $v$ into discrete and essential parts to get $acl(E)\subseteq G$.

nodes.name: Independence $E\ind^*_F G$
nodes.statement: Let $E$, $F$, $G\subseteq H$. We say that $E$ is \textit{independent} from $G$ over $F$ if for all $v\in E$ $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(F\cup G)}(v)$ and denote it $E\ind^*_F G$.

nodes.name: Elementary reformulations of $\ind^*$
nodes.statement: Let $\bv$, $\bw\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then it is easy to see that: \bitm \item $\bv$ is independent from $\bw$ over $\emptyset$ if and only if for every $j,k=1,\dots,n$, $H_{(v_j)_e}\perp H_{(w_k)_e}$. \item $\bv$ is independent from $\bw$ over $E$ if and only if for every $j,k=1,\dots,n$, $H_{P_E^\perp(v_j)_e}\perp H_{P_E^\perp(w_k)_e}$. \item $\bv\in H^n$ and $E$, $F\subseteq H$. Then $\bv\ind^*_EF$ if and only if for every $j=1,\dots,n$ $v_j\ind^*_EF$ that is, for all $j=1,\dots,n$ $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v_j)$. \eitm
nodes.statement_short: Independence of tuples reduces to orthogonality of the generated subrepresentations, and to coordinatewise independence.

nodes.name: Types over $\emptyset$ and isometric isomorphism of cyclic subrepresentations
nodes.statement: Let $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$. Then $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_w,\p_w,w)$, this is, the map sending $v$ to $w$ extends to a unique isometric isomorphism between $(H_v,\p_v)$ and $(H_w,\p_w)$.
nodes.statement_short: Two vectors have the same type over $\emptyset$ iff their cyclic subrepresentations are isometrically isomorphic.
conclusions: $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_w,\p_w,w)$

nodes.name: Characterization of non-forking extensions
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$, $p\in S_n(E)$ $q\in S_n(F)$ and $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$, $\bw=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ be such that $p=tp(\bv/E)$ and $q=tp(\bw/F)$. Then $q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bw\ind^*_EF$ if and only if the following conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(F)}(w_j)$ \item For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j)$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $q$ is an independent extension of $p$ iff the projections onto $acl$ agree coordinatewise and the orthogonal cyclic parts are isometrically isomorphic.
assumptions: Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$, $p\in S_n(E)$ $q\in S_n(F)$ and $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$, $\bw=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ be such that $p=tp(\bv/E)$ and $q=tp(\bw/F)$
$q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bw\ind^*_EF$
conclusions: For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(F)}(w_j)$

For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j)$

nodes.name: Proof of the characterization of non-forking extensions
nodes.statement: Clear from Theorem \ref{typeoverempty1} and Remark \ref{independenceoverempty}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the type-classification fact with the reformulation of independence.

nodes.name: $P^\perp_{acl(E)}v=(P^\perp_Ev)_e$
nodes.statement: Recall that for every $E\subseteq H$ and $v\in H$, $P^\perp_{acl(E)}v=(P^\perp_Ev)_e$.

nodes.statement: $\ind^*$ is a freeness relation.
conclusions: $\ind^*$ is a freeness relation

nodes.name: Proof that $\ind^*$ is a freeness relation
nodes.statement:
By Remark ef{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, to prove local character, finite character and transitivity it is enough to show them for the case of a 1-tuple.  egin{description} \item[Local character] Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq H$. Let $w=(P_{acl(E)}(v))_e$. Then there exist a sequence of $(l_k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq \N$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq \A$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq E$ such that if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\p(a_j^k)e_j^k$ for $k\in\N$, then $w_k	o w$ when $k	o\infty$. Let $E_0=\{e_j^k\ |\ j=1,\dots,l_k	ext{ and }k\in\N\}$. Then $v\ind_{E_0}^*E$ and $|E_0|=\aleph_0$. \item[Finite character] We show that for $v\in H$, $E,F\subseteq H$, $v\ind^*_EF$ if and only if $v\ind^*_EF_0$ for every finite $F_0\subseteq F$. The left to right direction is clear. For right to left, suppose that $v
ind^*_EF$. Let $w=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v)-P_{acl(E)}(v)$. Then $w\in$ acl$(E\cup F)\setminus$acl$(E)$. As in the proof of local character, there exist a sequence of pairs $(l_k,n_k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq \N^2$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k+n_k}^k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq \A$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k,f_1^k,\dots,f_{n_k}^k)_{k\in\N}$ such that $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)\subseteq E$, $(f_1^k,\dots,f_{n_k}^k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq F$ and if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\p(a_j^k)e_i^k+\sum_{j=1}^{n_k}\p(a_{l_k+j}^k)f_j^k$ for $k\in\N$, then $w_k	o w$ when $k	o\infty$. Since $v
ind^*_EF$, then $w=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v)-P_{acl(E)}(v)
eq 0$. Let $\e=\|w\|>0$. Then, there is $k_\e$ such that if $k\geq k_\e$ then $\|w-w_k\|<\e$. Let $F_0:=\{f_1^1,\dots,f_{k_\e}^{n_{k_\e}}\}$, then $F_0$ is a finite subset such that $v
ind^*_EF_0$. \item[Transitivity of independence] Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq F\subseteq G\subseteq H$. If $v\ind_E^*G$ then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. It is clear that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ so $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$. Conversely, if $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$, we have that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)$ and $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. Then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ and $v\ind_E^*G$. \item[Symmetry] It is clear from Remark ef{independenceoverA}. \item[Invariance] Let $U$ be an automorphism of $(H,\p)$. Let $ v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$,$ w=(w_1,\dots,w_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$ be such that $ v\ind_E^* w$. By Remark ef{independenceoverA}, this means that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_k)}$. It follows that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uv_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uw_k)}$ and, again by Remark ef{independenceoverA}, $Uv\ind_{acl(UE)}^*Uw$. \item[Existence] Let $(	ilde{H},	ilde{\p})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq 	ilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, there exists $q\in S_n(F)$ such that $q$ is a non-forking extension of $p$.  dc \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in 	ilde{H}$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$ and let $(H^\prime,\p^\prime,u):=(H_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},\p_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$. Then, by Fact ef{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\p}):=(H,\p)\oplus (H^\prime,\p^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\p)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem ef{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$. \item[Induction step] Now, let $ v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in 	ilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in 	ilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$. \edc \item[Stationarity] Let $(	ilde{H},	ilde{\p})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq 	ilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, if $q\in S_n(F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ then $q=p^\prime$, where $p^\prime$ is the $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ built in the proof of existence.  dc \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in H$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$, and let $q\in S(F)$ and $w\in H$ be such that $w\models q$. Let $v^\prime$ be as in previous item. Then, by Theorem ef{nonforkingextension} we have that:  egin{enumerate} \item $P_{acl(E)}v=P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ \item $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to both \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)\] and \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)\] \end{enumerate} This means that $P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ and $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)$ and, therefore $q=tp(v^\prime/F)=p^\prime$. \item[Induction step] Let $ v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})$, $ v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}^\prime)$ and $ w=(w_1,\dots,w_{n+1})\in	ilde{H}$ be such that $ v\models p$, $ v^\prime\models p^\prime$ and $ w\models q$. By transitivity, we have that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ and $tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. By induction hypothesis, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$ and let $U^\prime$ an automorphism of the monster model fixing $F$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U^\prime(v_j^\prime)=w_j^\prime$. Again by transitivity, $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)$ and $tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_{n+1}/Ev_1,\cdots v_n)$. By the case $n=1$ $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)=tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ and therefore $p^\prime=tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime v_{n+1}^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n,w_{n+1}/F)=q$. \edc \end{description}
nodes.statement_short: Verify the seven axioms (local/finite character, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence, stationarity) one by one, reducing to 1-tuples and inducting on $n$ for the last two.

nodes.name: Local character
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq H$. Let $w=(P_{acl(E)}(v))_e$. Then there exist a sequence of $(l_k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq \N$, a sequence of finite tuples $(a_1^k,\dots,a_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq \A$ and a sequence of finite tuples $(e_1^k,\dots,e_{l_k}^k)_{k\in\N}\subseteq E$ such that if $w_k:=\sum_{j=1}^{l_k}\p(a_j^k)e_j^k$ for $k\in\N$, then $w_k\to w$ when $k\to\infty$. Let $E_0=\{e_j^k\ |\ j=1,\dots,l_k\text{ and }k\in\N\}$. Then $v\ind_{E_0}^*E$ and $|E_0|=\aleph_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $(P_{acl(E)}v)_e$ by finite sums to build a countable $E_0$ with $v\ind^*_{E_0}E$.

nodes.name: Transitivity of independence
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ and $E\subseteq F\subseteq G\subseteq H$. If $v\ind_E^*G$ then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. It is clear that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ so $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$. Conversely, if $v\ind_E^*F$ and $v\ind_F^*G$, we have that $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(F)}(v)$ and $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$. Then $P_{acl(E)}(v)=P_{acl(G)}(v)$ and $v\ind_E^*G$.
nodes.statement_short: Chase equalities of the projections $P_{acl(\cdot)}(v)$ in both directions.

nodes.name: Symmetry
nodes.statement: It is clear from Remark \ref{independenceoverA}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the earlier remark.

nodes.name: Invariance
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be an automorphism of $(H,\p)$. Let $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$,$\bw=(w_1,\dots,w_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$ be such that $\bv\ind_E^*\bw$. By Remark \ref{independenceoverA}, this means that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_k)}$. It follows that for every $j$, $k=1,\dots,n$ $H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uv_j)}\perp H_{P^\perp_{acl(UE)}(Uw_k)}$ and, again by Remark \ref{independenceoverA}, $Uv\ind_{acl(UE)}^*Uw$.
nodes.statement_short: Automorphisms preserve the orthogonality condition, hence independence.

nodes.name: Existence
nodes.statement: Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\p})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, there exists $q\in S_n(F)$ such that $q$ is a non-forking extension of $p$. \bdc \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$ and let $(H^\prime,\p^\prime,u):=(H_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},\p_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$. Then, by Fact \ref{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\p}):=(H,\p)\oplus (H^\prime,\p^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\p)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$. \item[Induction step] Now, let $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in \tilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$. \edc
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$: for $n=1$ build $v^\prime$ inside an elementary extension; then extend one coordinate at a time.

nodes.name: Stationarity
nodes.statement: Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\p})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, if $q\in S_n(F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ then $q=p^\prime$, where $p^\prime$ is the $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ built in the proof of existence. \bdc \item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in H$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$, and let $q\in S(F)$ and $w\in H$ be such that $w\models q$. Let $v^\prime$ be as in previous item. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} we have that: \begin{enumerate} \item $P_{acl(E)}v=P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ \item $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to both \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)\] and \[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)\] \end{enumerate} This means that $P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ and $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\p_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)$ and, therefore $q=tp(v^\prime/F)=p^\prime$. \item[Induction step] Let $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})$, $\bv^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}^\prime)$ and $\bw=(w_1,\dots,w_{n+1})\in\tilde{H}$ be such that $\bv\models p$, $\bv^\prime\models p^\prime$ and $\bw\models q$. By transitivity, we have that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ and $tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. By induction hypothesis, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$ and let $U^\prime$ an automorphism of the monster model fixing $F$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U^\prime(v_j^\prime)=w_j^\prime$. Again by transitivity, $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)$ and $tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_{n+1}/Ev_1,\cdots v_n)$. By the case $n=1$ $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)=tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ and therefore $p^\prime=tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime v_{n+1}^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n,w_{n+1}/F)=q$. \edc
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$: uniqueness of the independent extension follows from the characterization theorem plus transitivity.

nodes.name: Stability criterion via an independence relation
nodes.statement: A first order continuous logic theory $T$ is stable if and only if there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity. In that case the relation $\ind^*$ coincides with non-forking.
nodes.statement_short: A continuous theory is stable iff it admits a freeness relation, which then is non-forking.
assumptions: A first order continuous logic theory $T$
conclusions: $T$ is stable if and only if there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity
In that case the relation $\ind^*$ coincides with non-forking
nodes.origin_citation: Ben Yaacov, Berenstein, Henson & Usvyatsov [BBHU], Theorem 14.14

nodes.name: $T_\p$ is superstable
nodes.statement: The theory $T_\p$ is superstable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking.
conclusions: The theory $T_\p$ is superstable
the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking

nodes.name: Proof that $T_\p$ is superstable
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation}, $T_\p$ is stable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking. To prove superstability, we have to show that for every $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H$, every $F\subseteq H$ and every $\e>0$, there exist a finite $F_0\subseteq F$ and $\bv^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime)\in H^n$ such that $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\e$ and $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}F$ for every $j\leq n$. As in the proof of local character, for $j=1,\dots,n$ let $(\ a_1^{jk},\dots,\ a_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\N}$, $(\ e_1^{jk},\dots,\ e_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\N}$, $w_j:=(P_{acl(E)}(v_j))_e$ and $(w_j^k)_{k\in\N}$ be such that $w_j^k:=\sum_{s=1}^{l_k}\p(a_s^{jk})\ e_s^{jk}$ for $k\in\N$, and $w_j^k\to w_j$. For $j=1,\dots,n$, let $K_j\in\N$ be such that $\|w_j-w_j^{K_j}\|<\e$, let $v_j^\prime:=(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_d+w_j^{K_j}$ and let $F_0^j=\{e_s^k\ |\ k\leq K_j\text{ and }s=1,\dots,l_k\}$. If we define $F_0:=U_{j=1}^nF_0^j$, then for every $j=1,\dots,n$ we have that $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}^*F$, $|F_0|<\aleph_0$ and $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\e$.
nodes.statement_short: Stability from the BBHU criterion, then $\aleph_0$-local character by finitely approximating each $(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_e$ within $\e$.

nodes.name: Stability from the criterion
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation}, $T_\p$ is stable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the BBHU stability criterion to the freeness relation $\ind^*$.

nodes.name: Reduce superstability to finite $\e$-approximation
nodes.statement: To prove superstability, we have to show that for every $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H$, every $F\subseteq H$ and every $\e>0$, there exist a finite $F_0\subseteq F$ and $\bv^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime)\in H^n$ such that $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\e$ and $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}F$ for every $j\leq n$.
nodes.statement_short: State the finite-$\e$-approximation form of superstability to be verified.

nodes.name: Build the approximating sequences
nodes.statement: As in the proof of local character, for $j=1,\dots,n$ let $(\ a_1^{jk},\dots,\ a_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\N}$, $(\ e_1^{jk},\dots,\ e_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\N}$, $w_j:=(P_{acl(E)}(v_j))_e$ and $(w_j^k)_{k\in\N}$ be such that $w_j^k:=\sum_{s=1}^{l_k}\p(a_s^{jk})\ e_s^{jk}$ for $k\in\N$, and $w_j^k\to w_j$.
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the local-character approximation of $(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_e$ by finite sums.

nodes.name: Truncate and conclude
nodes.statement: For $j=1,\dots,n$, let $K_j\in\N$ be such that $\|w_j-w_j^{K_j}\|<\e$, let $v_j^\prime:=(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_d+w_j^{K_j}$ and let $F_0^j=\{e_s^k\ |\ k\leq K_j\text{ and }s=1,\dots,l_k\}$. If we define $F_0:=U_{j=1}^nF_0^j$, then for every $j=1,\dots,n$ we have that $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}^*F$, $|F_0|<\aleph_0$ and $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\e$.
nodes.statement_short: Truncate at $K_j$ to get a finite base $F_0$ with $\e$-close independent copies.

nodes.name: Canonical base of a type
nodes.statement: Recall that a canonical base for a type $p$ is a minimal set over which $p$ does not fork.

nodes.name: Canonical bases are tuples of real elements
nodes.statement: Let $\bv=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then $Cb(tp(\bv/E)):=\{(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)\}$ is a canonical base for the type $tp(\bv/E)$.
nodes.statement_short: The tuple of projections $(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)$ is a canonical base for $tp(\bv/E)$.
conclusions: $Cb(tp(\bv/E)):=\{(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)\}$ is a canonical base for the type $tp(\bv/E)$

nodes.name: Proof of the canonical base description
nodes.statement: First of all, we consider the case of a 1-tuple. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} $tp(v/E)$ does not fork over $Cb(tp(v/E))$. Let $(v_k)_{k<\omega}$ a Morley sequence for $tp(v/E)$. We have to show that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, for every $k<\omega$ there is a vector $w_k$ such that $v_k=P_Ev+w_k$ and $w_k\perp acl(\{P_Ev\}\cup\{w_j\ |\ j< k\})$. This means that for every $k<\omega$, $w_k\in H_e$ and for all $j$, $k<\omega$, $H_{w_j}\perp H_{w_k}$. For $k<\omega$, let $v^\prime_k:=\frac{v_1+\cdots+v_k}{n}=P_Ev+\frac{w_1+\cdots+w_k}{n}$. Then for every $k<\omega$, $v^\prime_k\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. Since $v^\prime_k\to P_ev$ when $k\to\infty$, we have that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. For the case of a general $n$-tuple, by Remark \ref{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, it is enough to repeat the previous argument in every component of $\bv$.
nodes.statement_short: Average a Morley sequence to recover $P_Ev$ in the definable closure, then reduce the $n$-tuple case to coordinates.

nodes.name: The 1-tuple case via averaging a Morley sequence
nodes.statement: First of all, we consider the case of a 1-tuple. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} $tp(v/E)$ does not fork over $Cb(tp(v/E))$. Let $(v_k)_{k<\omega}$ a Morley sequence for $tp(v/E)$. We have to show that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, for every $k<\omega$ there is a vector $w_k$ such that $v_k=P_Ev+w_k$ and $w_k\perp acl(\{P_Ev\}\cup\{w_j\ |\ j< k\})$. This means that for every $k<\omega$, $w_k\in H_e$ and for all $j$, $k<\omega$, $H_{w_j}\perp H_{w_k}$. For $k<\omega$, let $v^\prime_k:=\frac{v_1+\cdots+v_k}{n}=P_Ev+\frac{w_1+\cdots+w_k}{n}$. Then for every $k<\omega$, $v^\prime_k\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. Since $v^\prime_k\to P_ev$ when $k\to\infty$, we have that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$.
nodes.statement_short: Averages of a Morley sequence converge to $P_Ev$, putting it in the definable closure.

nodes.name: Reduce the $n$-tuple case to coordinates
nodes.statement: For the case of a general $n$-tuple, by Remark \ref{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, it is enough to repeat the previous argument in every component of $\bv$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the 1-tuple argument coordinatewise.

nodes.statement: The theory $T_\p$ has weak elimination of imaginaries.
conclusions: The theory $T_\p$ has weak elimination of imaginaries

nodes.name: Positive functional on $\A$
nodes.statement: Let $\A^\prime$ be the dual space of $\A$. An element $\f\in\A^\prime$ is called \textit{positive} if $\f(a)\geq 0$ whenever $a\in\A$ is positive, i.e. there is $b\in\A$ such that $a=b^*b$. The set of positive functionals is denoted by $\A^\prime_+$.
differentia: $\f(a)\geq 0$ whenever $a\in\A$ is positive, i.e. there is $b\in\A$ such that $a=b^*b$

nodes.name: Vectors define positive linear functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\A$ be a $C^*$-algebra of operators on a Hilbert space $H$, and let $v\in H$. Then the function $\f_v$ on $\A$ such that for every $S\in\A$, $\f_v(S)=\langle Sv\,|\,v\rangle$ is a positive linear functional.
assumptions: Let $\A$ be a $C^*$-algebra of operators on a Hilbert space $H$, and let $v\in H$
conclusions: the function $\f_v$ on $\A$ such that for every $S\in\A$, $\f_v(S)=\langle Sv\,|\,v\rangle$ is a positive linear functional

nodes.name: Types over $\emptyset$ are classified by $\f_v$
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. Then $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\f_v=\f_w$, where $\f_v$ denotes the positive linear functional on $\A$ defined by $v$ as in Lemma \ref{vectorsdefinepositivelinearfunctionals}.
conclusions: $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\f_v=\f_w$

nodes.name: Orthogonality and domination of positive linear functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\f$ and $\psi$ be positive linear functionals on $\A$. \ben \item They are called \textit{orthogonal} ($\f\perp\psi$) if $\|\f-\psi\|=\|\f\|+\|\psi\|$. \item Also, $\f$ is called \textit{dominated} by $\psi$ ($\f\leq\psi$) if there exist $\gamma>0$ such that the functional $\gamma\psi-\f$ is positive. \een
nodes.statement_short: $\f\perp\psi$ means $\|\f-\psi\|=\|\f\|+\|\psi\|$; $\f\leq\psi$ means $\gamma\psi-\f$ is positive for some $\gamma>0$.
differentia: $\f$ is called \textit{dominated} by $\psi$ ($\f\leq\psi$) if there exist $\gamma>0$ such that the functional $\gamma\psi-\f$ is positive

nodes.name: Subrepresentation embedding is equivalent to domination of functionals
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. Then $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$ if and only if $\f_v\leq\f_w$.
nodes.statement_short: $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ embeds in $(H_w,\p_w,w)$ exactly when $\f_v$ is dominated by $\f_w$.
conclusions: $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$ if and only if $\f_v\leq\f_w$

nodes.name: Proof that embedding is equivalent to domination
nodes.statement: Suppose $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$. Then there exists a vector $v^\prime\in H_w$ such that $(H_v,\p_v,v)\simeq (H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$. By Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators (see \cite{Hen}), there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\p_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\p_v(\A)$. Let $\g=\|P\|^2$. Then, for every positive element $a\in\A$, $\f_{v}(a)=\f_{v^\prime}(a)=\langle \p(a)v^\prime\ |\ v^\prime\rangle=\langle \p(a)Pw\ |\ Pw\rangle=\langle P^*\p(a)Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle \p(a)\|P\|^2w\ |\ w\rangle\leq \g\langle \p(a)w\ |\ w\rangle=\g\f_{w}(a)$ which means that $\g\f_w-\f_{v}$ is positive and $\f_v\leq\f_w$. The converse is Corollary 3.3.8 in \cite{Pe}.
nodes.statement_short: Forward: get the Radon-Nikodym operator $P$ and take $\g=\|P\|^2$; converse quoted from Pedersen.

nodes.name: Forward direction via the Radon-Nikodym operator
nodes.statement: Suppose $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$. Then there exists a vector $v^\prime\in H_w$ such that $(H_v,\p_v,v)\simeq (H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$. By Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators (see \cite{Hen}), there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\p_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\p_v(\A)$. Let $\g=\|P\|^2$. Then, for every positive element $a\in\A$, $\f_{v}(a)=\f_{v^\prime}(a)=\langle \p(a)v^\prime\ |\ v^\prime\rangle=\langle \p(a)Pw\ |\ Pw\rangle=\langle P^*\p(a)Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle \p(a)\|P\|^2w\ |\ w\rangle\leq \g\langle \p(a)w\ |\ w\rangle=\g\f_{w}(a)$ which means that $\g\f_w-\f_{v}$ is positive and $\f_v\leq\f_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\f_v(a)\leq\|P\|^2\f_w(a)$ using the intertwining operator $P$.

nodes.name: Converse quoted from the literature
nodes.statement: The converse is Corollary 3.3.8 in \cite{Pe}.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Pedersen for the reverse implication.

nodes.name: Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators
nodes.statement: By Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators (see \cite{Hen}), there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\p_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\p_v(\A)$.
nodes.statement_short: An embedding of cyclic representations is implemented by a bounded positive intertwining operator.
conclusions: there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\p_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\p_v(\A)$
nodes.origin_citation: Henle [Hen], A Lebesgue decomposition theorem for $C^*$-algebras

nodes.name: Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction
nodes.statement: Let $\f$ be a positive functional on $\A$. Then there exists a cyclic representation $(H_\f,\p_\f,v_\f)$ such that for all $a\in\A$, $\f(a)=\langle \p_\f(a)v_\f|v_\f\rangle$. This representation is called the \textit{Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction}.
nodes.statement_short: Every positive functional is a vector state of a cyclic representation (GNS).
assumptions: Let $\f$ be a positive functional on $\A$
conclusions: there exists a cyclic representation $(H_\f,\p_\f,v_\f)$ such that for all $a\in\A$, $\f(a)=\langle \p_\f(a)v_\f|v_\f\rangle$

nodes.name: Orthogonal functionals give non-embeddable cyclic representations
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. If $\f_v\perp\f_w$, then $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$.
conclusions: $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$

nodes.name: Proof that $\f_v\perp\f_w$ blocks embeddings
nodes.statement: Suppose $\f_v\perp\f_w$, and $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $\f_v\leq\f_w$; let $\g>0$ be a real number such that $\g\f_w-\f_v$ is a bounded positive functional and let $u\in H$ be such that $\f_u=\g\f_w-\f_v$, which is possible by GNS Theorem. Then $\f_v=\g\f_w-\f_u$, and $\|\f_w-\f_v\|=\|\f_w-\g\f_w+\f_u\|=\|(1-\g)\f_w+\f_u\|=|1-\g|\|\f_w\|+\|\f_u\|\neq \|\f_w\|+\|\f_v\|$, but this contradicts $\f_v\perp\f_w$.

nodes.name: Set up the contradiction and the GNS witness
nodes.statement: Suppose $\f_v\perp\f_w$, and $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $\f_v\leq\f_w$; let $\g>0$ be a real number such that $\g\f_w-\f_v$ is a bounded positive functional and let $u\in H$ be such that $\f_u=\g\f_w-\f_v$, which is possible by GNS Theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Assume an embedding, get $\f_v\leq\f_w$ and realize $\g\f_w-\f_v$ as $\f_u$ by GNS.

nodes.name: Norm computation contradicting orthogonality

nodes.name: Disjoint representations
nodes.statement: Recall that two representations are said to be \textit{disjoint} if they do not have any common subrepresentation up to isometric isomorphism.
differentia: they do not have any common subrepresentation up to isometric isomorphism

nodes.name: Disjoint subrepresentations have complementary central projections
nodes.statement: Two subrepresentations $(H_1,\p_1)$, $(H_2,\p_2)$ of $(H,\p)$ are disjoint if and only if there is a projection $P$ in $\p(\A)^\prime\cap \p(\A)^{\prime\prime}$ such that if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the projections on $H_1$ and $H_2$ respectively, we have that $PP_1=P_1$ and $(I-P)P_2=P_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness is witnessed by a central projection separating the two subspaces.
conclusions: are disjoint if and only if there is a projection $P$ in $\p(\A)^\prime\cap \p(\A)^{\prime\prime}$ such that if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the projections on $H_1$ and $H_2$ respectively, we have that $PP_1=P_1$ and $(I-P)P_2=P_2$
nodes.origin_citation: Connes [Co], Noncommutative geometry, Chapter 5, Section 2, Proposition 3

nodes.name: The strong closure of $\p(\A)$ is its double commutant
nodes.statement: Let $\A$ be a $C^*$algebra and $\p:\A\to B(H)$ a nondegenerate representation of $\A$. Let $\MM$ be the strong closure of $\pi(\A)$. Then $\MM$ is weakly closed and $\MM=\A^{\prime\prime}$.
assumptions: Let $\A$ be a $C^*$algebra and $\p:\A\to B(H)$ a nondegenerate representation of $\A$
Let $\MM$ be the strong closure of $\pi(\A)$
conclusions: $\MM$ is weakly closed and $\MM=\A^{\prime\prime}$

nodes.name: Kaplanski densitiy theorem
nodes.statement: Let $\A$ be a $C^*$-subalgebra of $B(H)$ with strong closure $\MM$. Then the unit ball $Ball_1(\A)$ of $\A$ is strongly dense in the unit ball $Ball_1(\MM)$ of $\MM$. Furthermore, the set of selfadjoint elements in $Ball_1(\A)$ is strongly dense in the set of selfadjoint elements of $Ball_1(\MM)$.
nodes.statement_short: The unit ball of a $C^*$-subalgebra is strongly dense in that of its strong closure (also for selfadjoints).
assumptions: Let $\A$ be a $C^*$-subalgebra of $B(H)$ with strong closure $\MM$
conclusions: the unit ball $Ball_1(\A)$ of $\A$ is strongly dense in the unit ball $Ball_1(\MM)$ of $\MM$
the set of selfadjoint elements in $Ball_1(\A)$ is strongly dense in the set of selfadjoint elements of $Ball_1(\MM)$

nodes.name: $\e$-characterization of orthogonality of positive functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\f$ and $\psi$ be two positive linear functionals on $\A$. Then, $\f\perp\psi$ if and only if for all $\e>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\A$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\f(e-a)<\e$ and $\psi(a)<\e$.
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality is equivalent to the existence of almost-separating positive contractions.
assumptions: Let $\f$ and $\psi$ be two positive linear functionals on $\A$
conclusions: $\f\perp\psi$ if and only if for all $\e>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\A$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\f(e-a)<\e$ and $\psi(a)<\e$

nodes.name: Orthogonality passes to dominated functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\f_1$, $\f_2$, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ be positive linear functionals on $\A$ such that $\f_1\leq\f_2$ and $\psi_1\leq\psi_2$. If $\f_2\perp\psi_2$, then $\f_1\perp\psi_1$.
assumptions: Let $\f_1$, $\f_2$, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ be positive linear functionals on $\A$ such that $\f_1\leq\f_2$ and $\psi_1\leq\psi_2$
conclusions: $\f_1\perp\psi_1$

nodes.name: Proof that orthogonality passes to dominated functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\g_1>0$ and $\g_2>0$ be such that $\g_1\f_2-\f_1$ and $\g_2\psi_2-\psi_1$ are positive. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, for $\e>0$ there exists a positive $a\in\A$ with norm less than or equal to $1$ such that $\f_2(e-a)<\frac{\e}{\g_1+\g_2}$ and $\psi_2(a)<\frac{\e}{\g_1+\g_2}$. Then $\f_1(e-a)\leq\g_1\f_2(e-a)<\frac{\g_1\e}{\g_1+\g_2}<\e$ and $\psi_1(a)\leq\g_2\psi_2(a)<\frac{\g_2\e}{\g_1+\g_2}<\e$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the $\e$-criterion to the dominating pair and rescale $\e$ by $\g_1+\g_2$.

nodes.name: Choose the almost-separating element for the dominating pair
nodes.statement: Let $\g_1>0$ and $\g_2>0$ be such that $\g_1\f_2-\f_1$ and $\g_2\psi_2-\psi_1$ are positive. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, for $\e>0$ there exists a positive $a\in\A$ with norm less than or equal to $1$ such that $\f_2(e-a)<\frac{\e}{\g_1+\g_2}$ and $\psi_2(a)<\frac{\e}{\g_1+\g_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $\g_i$ from domination and apply the $\e$-criterion with $\e/(\g_1+\g_2)$.

nodes.name: Estimate the dominated functionals
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\f_1(e-a)$ and $\psi_1(a)$ by $\e$.

nodes.name: Orthogonality of $\f_v,\f_w$ versus disjointness of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$, $(H_w,\p_w,w)$
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. $\f_v\perp\f_w$ if and only if no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\f_v\perp\f_w$ exactly when the cyclic representations generated by $v$ and $w$ are disjoint.
conclusions: $\f_v\perp\f_w$ if and only if no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$

nodes.name: Proof of the orthogonality-disjointness equivalence
nodes.statement: Suppose $\f_v\perp\f_w$. By Lemma \ref{phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2}, if $(H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ and $(H_{w^\prime},\p_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$, then $\f_{v^\prime}\perp\f_{w^\prime}$, By Lemma \ref{phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic}, $(H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{w^\prime},\p_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$, and the conclusion follows. Conversely, suppose no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$. Then the representations $(H_v,\p_v)$ and $(H_w,\p_w)$ are disjoint. By Fact \ref{FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections}, there is a projection $P\in\p(\A)^\prime\cap\p(\A)^{\prime\prime}$ such that $PP_v=P_v$ and $(I-P)P_w=P_w$. Then, $\f_v(I-P)=\langle (I-P)v\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-PP_vv)\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-v)\ |\ v\rangle=0$. On the other hand, $\f_w(P)=\langle Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(w-Pw)\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)w\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-w\ |\ w\rangle=0$. By Fact \ref{FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA} and Theorem \ref{TheoremKaplansky}, the projection $P$ is strongly approximable by positive elements in $\p(\A)$ and therefore, for $\e>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\A$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\f_v(e-a)<\e$ and $\f_w(a)<\e$. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, $\f_v\perp\f_w$.
nodes.statement_short: Forward via hereditary orthogonality; converse by producing a central projection and approximating it with Kaplansky density to apply the $\e$-criterion.

nodes.name: Forward direction: orthogonality is hereditary
nodes.statement: Suppose $\f_v\perp\f_w$. By Lemma \ref{phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2}, if $(H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ and $(H_{w^\prime},\p_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$, then $\f_{v^\prime}\perp\f_{w^\prime}$, By Lemma \ref{phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic}, $(H_{v^\prime},\p_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{w^\prime},\p_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$, and the conclusion follows.
nodes.statement_short: Pass orthogonality down to subrepresentations, then block isomorphism.

nodes.name: Converse: central projection plus Kaplansky approximation
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\p_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\p_w,w)$. Then the representations $(H_v,\p_v)$ and $(H_w,\p_w)$ are disjoint. By Fact \ref{FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections}, there is a projection $P\in\p(\A)^\prime\cap\p(\A)^{\prime\prime}$ such that $PP_v=P_v$ and $(I-P)P_w=P_w$. Then, $\f_v(I-P)=\langle (I-P)v\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-PP_vv)\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-v)\ |\ v\rangle=0$. On the other hand, $\f_w(P)=\langle Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(w-Pw)\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)w\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-w\ |\ w\rangle=0$. By Fact \ref{FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA} and Theorem \ref{TheoremKaplansky}, the projection $P$ is strongly approximable by positive elements in $\p(\A)$ and therefore, for $\e>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\A$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\f_v(e-a)<\e$ and $\f_w(a)<\e$. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, $\f_v\perp\f_w$.
nodes.statement_short: From disjointness get a central projection annihilating both functionals, approximate it in $\p(\A)$, and apply the $\e$-criterion.

nodes.name: Almost orthogonality of types over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $\f_{v_e}\perp \f_{w_e}$.

nodes.name: Characterization of almost orthogonality over a set $E$
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp_E^a q$ if and only if $\f_{P^\perp_E(v_e)}\perp \f_{P^\perp_E(w_e)}$
nodes.statement_short: Almost orthogonality over $E$ corresponds to orthogonality of the functionals of the $E$-orthogonal essential parts.
assumptions: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\perp_E^a q$ if and only if $\f_{P^\perp_E(v_e)}\perp \f_{P^\perp_E(w_e)}$

nodes.name: Almost orthogonality coincides with orthogonality
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$. Then, $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $p\perp q$.
conclusions: $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $p\perp q$

nodes.name: Proof that $\perp^a$ coincides with $\perp$
nodes.statement: Assume $p\perp^a q$, $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$ are small subsets of the monster model and $p^\prime$, $q^\prime\in S_1(F)$ are non-forking extensions of $p$ and $q$ respectively. Let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p^\prime$ and $w\models q^\prime$, then $\f_{P^\perp_F(v_e)}=\f_{P^\perp_Ev_e}\perp\f_{P^\perp_Ew_e}=\f_{P^\perp_F(w_e)}$. By Lemma \ref{orthogonalityoverempty}, this implies that $p^\prime\perp^a q^\prime$. Therefore $p\perp q$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Almost orthogonality is preserved by non-forking extensions, so it upgrades to full orthogonality.

nodes.name: Almost orthogonality persists in non-forking extensions
nodes.statement: Assume $p\perp^a q$, $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$ are small subsets of the monster model and $p^\prime$, $q^\prime\in S_1(F)$ are non-forking extensions of $p$ and $q$ respectively. Let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p^\prime$ and $w\models q^\prime$, then $\f_{P^\perp_F(v_e)}=\f_{P^\perp_Ev_e}\perp\f_{P^\perp_Ew_e}=\f_{P^\perp_F(w_e)}$. By Lemma \ref{orthogonalityoverempty}, this implies that $p^\prime\perp^a q^\prime$. Therefore $p\perp q$.
nodes.statement_short: Projections are unchanged along non-forking extensions, so $p^\prime\perp^a q^\prime$.

nodes.name: Trivial converse
nodes.statement: The converse is trivial.

nodes.name: Domination of types over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$ and let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$ if and only if $\f_{w_e}\leq\f_{v_e}$.
assumptions: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$ and let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$ if and only if $\f_{w_e}\leq\f_{v_e}$

nodes.name: Proof of domination over $\emptyset$
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$. Suppose that $v^\prime$ and $w^\prime$ are such that $v^\prime\models p$, $w^ \prime\models q$ and if $v^\prime\ind^*_\emptyset E$ then $w^\prime\ind_\emptyset^*E$ for every $E$. Then for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev^\prime_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This implies that $w^\prime_e\in H_{v^\prime_e}$, and $H_{w^\prime_e}\subseteq H_{v^\prime_e}$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw}, $\f_{w_e}=\f_{w^\prime_e}\leq\f_{v^\prime_e}=\f_{v_e}$. For the converse, suppose $\f_{w_e}\leq\f_{v_e}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $H_{w_e}$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $H_{v_e}$, which implies that there is $w^\prime\in H_v$ such that $w^\prime\models tp(w/\emptyset)$ and for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This means than $tp(w/\emptyset)\vartriangleleft_\emptyset tp(v/\emptyset)$.
nodes.statement_short: Translate domination into containment $H_{w_e}\subseteq H_{v_e}$ of generated subrepresentations and apply the embedding-domination theorem in both directions.

nodes.name: Forward direction: domination gives containment
nodes.statement: Suppose $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$. Suppose that $v^\prime$ and $w^\prime$ are such that $v^\prime\models p$, $w^ \prime\models q$ and if $v^\prime\ind^*_\emptyset E$ then $w^\prime\ind_\emptyset^*E$ for every $E$. Then for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev^\prime_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This implies that $w^\prime_e\in H_{v^\prime_e}$, and $H_{w^\prime_e}\subseteq H_{v^\prime_e}$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw}, $\f_{w_e}=\f_{w^\prime_e}\leq\f_{v^\prime_e}=\f_{v_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Domination forces $H_{w_e}\subseteq H_{v_e}$, hence $\f_{w_e}\leq\f_{v_e}$.

nodes.name: Converse: build a dominated realization
nodes.statement: For the converse, suppose $\f_{w_e}\leq\f_{v_e}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $H_{w_e}$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $H_{v_e}$, which implies that there is $w^\prime\in H_v$ such that $w^\prime\models tp(w/\emptyset)$ and for every $E\subseteq H$ \[P_Ev_e=0\Rightarrow P_Ew^\prime_e=0\] This means than $tp(w/\emptyset)\vartriangleleft_\emptyset tp(v/\emptyset)$.
nodes.statement_short: From $\f_{w_e}\leq\f_{v_e}$ realize $q$ inside $H_v$, giving domination.

nodes.name: Characterization of domination of stationary types over $G$
nodes.statement: Let $E$, $F$ and $G$ be small subsets of $\tilde{H}$ such that $E$, $F\subseteq G$ and $p\in S_1(E)$ and $q\in S_1(F)$ be two stationary types. Then $p\vartriangleright_G q$ if and only if there exist $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$ such that $tp(v/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $p$, $tp(w/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $q$ and $\f_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}w_e}\leq\f_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}v_e}$.
nodes.statement_short: Domination over $G$ is equivalent to domination of the functionals of the $acl(G)$-orthogonal essential parts of suitable realizations.

conclusions: $p\vartriangleright_G q$ if and only if there exist $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$ such that $tp(v/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $p$, $tp(w/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $q$ and $\f_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}w_e}\leq\f_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}v_e}$
